query: Earlier W-based high-entropy alloys showed promising microstructural stability, high-temperature strength, and irradiation tolerance, but most contained Nb, Mo, Cr, or Ni, whose activation behavior and other service limitations restrict their suitability for plasma-facing components. Candidate structural materials must combine thermal and mechanical performance with low neutron activation and rapid radioactive decay. The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy uses refractory, relatively low-activation constituents and has shown creep and molten-salt-corrosion resistance, yet its plastic strain and toughness remain unreported and poorly understood. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs its plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the hypothesized cause, the observations predicted relative to pure tungsten, the boundaries of validity, the cited prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The equimolar WTaTiVZr high‐entropy alloy (HEA) exhibits greater plastic strain and fracture toughness than pure tungsten under high‐temperature plasma‐facing‐component (PFC) service because its high configurational entropy stabilizes a single‐phase BCC solid solution in which uniformly distributed solute atoms at grain boundaries suppress embrittling segregation and the multi‐element lattice promotes heterogeneous dislocation activity that blunts crack tips and enables uniform plastic flow.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar WTaTiVZr HEA, single‐phase BCC, equiaxed grains (~10 μm), no detectable secondary phases
generation.intervention: High‐temperature mechanical testing: uniaxial tensile tests and fracture toughness (compact tension) tests at 1000 °C in vacuum (~10⁻⁶ Torr)
generation.conditions: Temperature=1000 °C; vacuum pressure≈10⁻⁶ Torr; tensile strain rate=10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; matched initial grain size (~10 μm) in HEA and pure W
generation.mechanism: High configurational entropy enforces uniform solute distribution at grain boundaries, reducing grain‐boundary embrittlement, while lattice distortion from multiple principal elements increases the propensity for cross‐slip and dislocation interactions that blunt advancing cracks and enable extensive plastic deformation
generation.predicted_outcome: Under identical test conditions, WTaTiVZr will display total elongation >20% and fracture toughness KIc>30 MPa√m, whereas pure W will show <5% elongation and KIc<20 MPa√m, with HEA exhibiting predominantly transgranular ductile fracture and W showing brittle intergranular fracture
generation.baseline: Commercial‐grade pure tungsten tested under the same high‐temperature conditions
generation.boundary: Valid for equimolar, single‐phase WTaTiVZr with ~10 μm grains at 800–1200 °C; not necessarily valid for other compositions, multi‐phase microstructures, grain sizes outside ~1–100 μm, or temperatures below the ductile‐to‐brittle transition (~400 °C)
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—no prior direct measurements of plasticity in this specific HEA composition are reported

falsification_experiment.design: Produce equimolar WTaTiVZr and pure W samples with ~10 μm grain size. Perform tensile tests at 1000 °C in 10⁻⁶ Torr vacuum at 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ to failure and compact‐tension fracture toughness tests under the same conditions. Characterize fracture surfaces by SEM to determine mode.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If WTaTiVZr exhibits ≤10% elongation or ≤25 MPa√m KIc, or shows predominantly intergranular brittle fracture similar to pure W, the hypothesis is falsified.
